title: Geneva Bible (1560) - Tables, Pages 1201-1224
author: Unknown
description: The concluding tables (pages 1201-1224) of the 1560 Geneva Bible. These finding aids accompany the scripture text. 'The first table' is an alphabetical interpretation of Hebrew, Chaldean, Greek and Latin proper names, giving each name's meaning and a scriptural reference (for example 'Ishmael, God hath heard, Gen. 16'; 'Israel, a prince of God, or prevailing with God'). The second table is a topical index of 'the principal things' contained in the Bible, with references, and there are calendrical and reference materials. Written in sixteenth-century orthography, these tables show how the Reformation translators equipped lay readers for personal study and give onomastic interpretations that are of interest for biblical symbolism. It is a companion to the library's other Geneva Bible files.
editionNote: Curator-supplied PDF and EPUB from the organised ebook collection. One format was converted from the other (PDF from EPUB).
rights: Scan of the 1560 Geneva Bible text; the underlying work is public domain. The rights status of this particular scan/OCR has not been confirmed.
